body: {"total":5,"records":[{"title":"One-hour high-sensitivity troponin rule-out pathways in the emergency department: a systematic review and meta-analysis of safety","authors":"Achebe-Lindgren O, Marchetti-Soyinka P, Hallam-Oduya R","year":2022,"venue":"Emergency Cardiac Care Reviews","doi":"10.5555/eccr.2022.0133","providerType":"review","abstract":"We searched four databases to June 2021 for studies applying a 0/1-hour high-sensitivity troponin algorithm to adults presenting with suspected myocardial infarction. Twenty-two studies with 31,400 patients were included. Among patients ruled out at one hour (pooled 57 percent of those tested), the 30-day rate of death or myocardial infarction was 0.3 percent (95 percent CI 0.2 to 0.5). Sensitivity for index myocardial infarction was 98.8 percent. Most studies were prospective validation studies in specialist centres; eight had a high risk of bias in patient selection, and few reported results by age or kidney function."},{"title":"Moving from a three-hour to a one-hour troponin pathway in a district hospital chest pain unit: a before-after evaluation","authors":"Kowalczyk-Ames B, Ferreira-Olatunji D","year":2019,"venue":"District Hospital Medicine","providerType":"journal-article","abstract":"We compared 12 months before and 12 months after a switch from a 0/3-hour to a 0/1-hour high-sensitivity troponin pathway in a 480-bed district hospital. Median time in the department for ruled-out patients fell from 7.2 to 4.1 hours, and the proportion discharged directly from the unit rose from 41 to 55 percent. Among patients discharged after rule-out, the 30-day rate of death or myocardial infarction was 0.4 percent before and 0.3 percent after. In the first three months the second sample was drawn outside the 45 to 75 minute window in 22 percent of patients, falling to 9 percent after a phlebotomy prompt was added."},{"title":"Timing of the second troponin sample and laboratory turnaround under rapid rule-out algorithms: an observational study","authors":"Srinivasan-Holt M, Eriksen-Obi A, Tulloch-Mensah J","year":2021,"venue":"Laboratory Medicine in Practice","doi":"10.5555/lmp.2021.0217","providerType":"journal-article","abstract":"Across three emergency departments using a 0/1-hour algorithm, we recorded sample collection and result times for 5,812 patients. The second sample was collected outside the 45 to 75 minute window in 18 percent of patients, most often during the afternoon peak. Median laboratory turnaround was 52 minutes and exceeded 90 minutes for 11 percent of samples. When the second sample was late, the algorithm placed more patients in the observe zone, and 3 of 1,040 late-sampled patients who were ruled out had a myocardial infarction within 30 days. The authors recommend timed prompts and escalation when turnaround exceeds one hour."},{"title":"Performance of a one-hour troponin rule-out algorithm in patients aged 75 or over and in chronic kidney disease","authors":"Beaumont-Adeyinka C, Yamada-Rourke L, Pereira-Strand K, Owusu-Fairley E","year":2023,"venue":"Emergency Cardiac Care Reviews","doi":"10.5555/eccr.2023.0271","providerType":"journal-article","abstract":"In a multicentre prospective study of 9,760 patients, we examined the 0/1-hour algorithm in patients aged 75 or over (n=2,310) and in those with an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 60 (n=1,480). Sensitivity for myocardial infarction remained above 97 percent in both groups, but only 29 percent of older patients and 21 percent of patients with kidney disease were ruled out at one hour, compared with 62 percent of younger patients with normal kidney function. More than half of both groups fell into the observe zone and needed a third sample. Age-adjusted thresholds increased rule-out but lowered sensitivity."},{"title":"Early discharge after one-hour troponin rule-out and 30-day outcomes in a regional network: conference abstract","authors":"Oyewole-Brandt S, Kilbride-Nakamura T","year":2025,"venue":"Regional Cardiac Society annual meeting abstract book","providerType":"conference-abstract","abstract":"This abstract reports early discharge after a 0/1-hour rule-out across five hospitals in one region. Of 14,200 patients tested, 7,950 were ruled out and discharged within four hours. The 30-day rate of death or myocardial infarction among them was reported as 0.2 percent. Methods for follow-up were not described, it is unclear whether patients who attended hospitals outside the region were captured, and no full report has been published. Results by age and kidney function were not given, and the abstract does not say how many patients left before the second sample was taken."}]}
